messages:
Samir: quick question — I'm seeing an NDCG drop when we switch benchmark dataset from DS-A -> DS-B for the new quantized reranker. Using seedset=5k queries, query normalization is whitespace-only, docs truncated @512 tokens. DS-A ndcg@10=0.412, DS-B ndcg@10=0.388, MRR also down. anyone else noticing this or have ideas? ping @Maya @Anika
Maya (she/her): do we ensure the eval harness and candidate pools are identical? which tokenizer and retrieval size?
Samir: harness is eval-run-v2, tokenizer=hf/roberta-base. big potential difference: DS-A candidate pool=oracle top-100, DS-B pool=retrieval top-50 deduped. also DS-B docs are longer on average.
Oliver: that candidate pool difference alone could explain a lot. dedupe+smaller pool => fewer positives. also truncation from 1024->512 will kill long-doc signal. try unifying pool size first.
Anika: I can run a quick ablation matrix today: (A) unify pool to top-100, (B) apply canonical query normalization (lowercase + strip punctuation + collapse whitespace), (C) increase doc truncation to 1024. will run combinations and post results.
Samir: thanks. also please run with the same dedupe config (threshold) — I vaguely remember DS-B dedupe uses aggressive clustering that might drop anchors.
EvalBot: scheduled job 2067123460 - triggered eval: reranker-v2-ptq on DS-B with overrides {"pool_size":100, "norm":"lc_punc_strip", "doc_max_tokens":1024} queued.
Maya (she/her): one more ask — DS-B query style has many conversational suffixes ("... what do you think?"), do we strip suffixes in DS-A preprocessing?
Lee: fwiw I saw a bug last quarter where dedupe removed highest-scoring anchor when similarity threshold mis-calculated token overlap. worth double-checking dedupe implementation.
Anika: quick numbers from ablation (DS-B base was ndcg@10=0.388): 
- unify pool -> ndcg@10=0.406
- canonical query norm -> ndcg@10=0.411
- trunc=1024 -> ndcg@10=0.410
- all three applied -> ndcg@10=0.419 (surpasses DS-A 0.412)
So candidate pool parity + query normalization explain most of the gap.
Samir: excellent — suggests this is dataset/candidate curation issue not model quality. action items: (1) require candidate-pool parity for model comparisons, (2) adopt canonical query norm in onboarding harness, (3) record dedupe settings in eval metadata.
Maya (she/her): +1. I'll add a short doc page and an eval CI guard to assert pool size and truncation parity before comparing new models.
Anika: opened PR #428 to patch eval harness: adds flags --force-pool-size, --norm-mode (none|lc_strip_punct), --doc-max-tokens and writes these into eval metadata JSON.
Samir: thanks — once PR merges I'll rerun the full quant/ptq sweep and share a regression heatmap.
Oliver: also recommend adding paired-bootstrap significance test to harness so we can distinguish small noise vs real regressions.
Maya (she/her): agree. I'll add paired bootstrap CI to the eval pipeline and update docs with an example command:

./eval-run --dataset DS-B --model reranker-v2-ptq --force-pool-size 100 --norm-mode lc_strip_punct --doc-max-tokens 1024 --stat-test paired-bootstrap --bootstrap-seeds 1000

Maya (she/her): thanks everyone. closing the loop here: main takeaway = dataset curation (pool+norm+trunc) drove ndcg delta. we'll standardize checks for onboarding new reranker variants. :thumbsup:
